cases.description: Both numbers are exactly equal; the absolute difference is 0 which is less than 1e-12, so the method should return true.

Numbers differ by 1e-12 (exactly the threshold). Since the implementation uses a strict '<' comparison, a difference of 1e-12 is *not* less than the threshold, thus this case actually returns false. Adjusted to a difference slightly smaller than the threshold.
Numbers differ by 1e-13, which is smaller than 1e-12, so the method should return true.
Numbers differ by 1e-12 exactly; because the comparison is '<' (strictly less), the method should return false.
Numbers differ by 1e-11, which is greater than the threshold, so the method should return false.
Both arguments are NaN; any arithmetic with NaN yields NaN, and the comparison with '<' evaluates to false, so the method should return false.
Both arguments are positive infinity; subtraction results in NaN, leading to a false comparison, so the method should return false.
Both arguments are negative infinity; same reasoning as positive infinity, the method should return false.
One argument is positive infinity and the other is negative infinity; the difference is infinite, so the method should return false.
Negative zero and positive zero are numerically equal; the absolute difference is 0, which is less than the 1e-12 threshold.
The smallest positive subnormal double (≈4.9e-324) differs from zero by far less than 1e-12, so the method should return true.
Two identical maximum finite double values have a difference of 0, which satisfies the < 1e-12 condition.
Subtracting an extremely tiny amount from Double.MAX_VALUE does not change its value due to rounding; the two arguments are effectively equal, yielding true.
The absolute difference is 2e-13, which is smaller than the 1e-12 tolerance, so the method should return true.
Any comparison involving NaN results in false; the method should return false when one argument is NaN.
Positive infinity minus a finite number yields infinity, whose absolute difference is not less than the threshold, so false is returned.
Negative infinity compared with a finite number also results in a difference that is not less than 1e-12, leading to false.
Two identical large negative double values have zero difference, satisfying the < 1e-12 condition.
The numbers differ by exactly 1e-12 (the threshold) but the method uses a strict '<', so it should return false.
